This letter is written in behalf of my wife, Charlotte F. BENJAMIN NADEL & COMPANY CERTIFIED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANTS 212-683-0071 437 FIFTH AVENUE NEW YORK, N.Y. 10016 PAUL SKWIERSKY, P.C. JACK SCHATTEN NORMAN NADEL NORMAN ALPERT NEIL BRESSLER DAVID G. BOTWINICK BENJAMIN NADEL COUNSEL September 23, 1986 Municipal Assistance Corporation One World Trade Center New York, New York 10047 Gentlemen: This letter is written in behalf of my wife, Charlotte F. Nadel, who uses our home address, 30 Barstow Road, Great Neck, New York 11021. In 1976 she purchased through The Chase Manhattan Bank a bond issued by you,
Denomination$5,000
SeriesCC 10 1/4%
No.40078
Dated11/1/76Payable2/1/93
As each interest coupon matured it was presented for payment and honored timely through February 1, 1986. The coupon payable on August 1, 1986 presented in the same manner was dishonored and returned stamped "Bond Called". This was the first time that she had any knowledge that this bond had been called. I had no knowledge of any call and made inquiry for her. Information provided to me indicated that this bond was called in 1984 for the Sinking Fund. Nevertheless, certainly aware of the call, your paying agent honored all of the interest coupons after the call date until August 1, 1986. On August 15, 1986 the bond was delivered to the National Westminster Bank USA, Great Neck Branch (36) for collection. Your paying agent remitted only $3,975, recouping for itself the four interest payments made through its clerical or other mistake, $1,025. During these two and one-half years you had the benefit of the use of $5,000 and the bondholder suffered the detriment of not having the use of the $5,000 for a replacement investment. Hence, in this situation of mutual mistake there is clearly unjust enrichment on your part which calls for suitable recompense to my wife. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Alumni | CUNY Graduate Center (https://www.gc.cuny.edu/mathematics/alumni) 【turn777709568search0】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 weeks ago; | On the Arithmetic and Geometry of Quaternion Algebras: A spectral correspondence of Mass Waveforms ... L111: 【60†Archives & Special Collections Collection, 1966-2001】 L112: This collection documents the establishment of an archival repository at Hunter College. The files of professors Dorothy G. Fowler, Frederic W. Stewart, Rose Gilligan, William Omelchenko, Lee E. Sellers, and Julio L. Hernandez-Delgado underscore their foresight and commitment to acquire, organize, preserve, and provide access to the historical documents of Hunter College. The collection consists of annual reports, correspondence, memoranda, and reports. L113: 【61†Tea & Talk Series Collection, 1967-1987】 L114: The Tea & Talk Program, co-sponsored by the Division of Programs in Education and the Hunter College Library, provided students and faculty with an opportunity to meet with prominent authors and illustrators of children and young adult books like Isaac Asimov, Pura Belpre, Norman Cousins, Virginia Hamilton, Maurice Sendak, John Steptoe, and others. Included are correspondence, announcements, cassette tapes, transcripts, and photographs of each invited speaker. L115: 【62†Margaret Grant Plumb Collection, 1890-1976】 L116: Margaret Grant Plumb graduated from Hunter College in 1916 and subsequently worked at her alma mater as a librarian/administrator for 44 years. Plumb was instrumental in gathering and preserving historical documents of the College and library that eventually served as a basis for the establishment of an archival repository at Hunter College in 1966. The collection primarily documents the establishment and evolution of library service at the Normal/ Hunter College Library from 1890 to 1960. L117: Key components of this collection are the library annual reports (1900 - 1951), records on the Bronx Campus Library (1928 - 1960) and the Park Avenue Library(1890 - 1950), papers pertaining to Margaret Grant Plumb (1911 - 1975), black and white photographs of the original Normal/Hunter College edifice (1873 - 1936) and the Park Avenue building (1940 - 1982), rare books(1932 - 1958), and materials pertaining to Dr. Margaret Barclay Wilson (Class of 1884), Honorary Librarian from 1915 to 1927.
